title: Day 974: 25 Days to Supreme Court July 1 October 7 Accountability Ruling — Kallner Bill Stalled; Accountability Crisis Deepens Amid Haredi Judicial Attack Fallout
detail: On June 7, 2026 (Day 974 / Ceasefire Day 241), Israel entered the final 25-day countdown to the Supreme Court's July 1, 2026 deadline, by which date the government must have demonstrated a credible October 7 accountability framework or face judicial intervention. The High Court of Justice's April 27, 2026 order granting a 2-month extension was explicit: the court would rule by July 1 whether the Netanyahu government had established a constitutionally adequate investigation mechanism. As of June 7, no such mechanism exists: the coalition's Kallner inquiry bill requires three more Knesset plenum readings, has been stripped of the phrase 'full, thorough, and independent investigation' from its purpose clause, bars judges from the commission, and requires 80 Knesset members to approve each of its 6-7 members — provisions legal advisers say are designed to ensure political control rather than genuine accountability. The aftermath of the June 3-6 Haredi attack on Supreme Court Deputy President Sohlberg's home, combined with Habima Square accountability protests (June 6), Netanyahu's appointment of his personal lawyer Michael Rabello as state comptroller, and the Board of Peace's stalled $17B reconstruction funding, had converged into the deepest institutional crisis in Israel's post-October 7 history. The Beyachad alliance (Bennett-Lapid) — polling ahead of Likud in some surveys — has pledged a Day 1 state commission of inquiry. Early elections are expected within five months following the May 20 preliminary dissolution vote. 63–72% of Israelis (JPPI/Hebrew University) support an independent commission. Bereaved families continue weekly protests outside Netanyahu's residence.

media.caption: 25 days to Supreme Court July 1 deadline — Kallner bill stripped of independence language, Haredi judicial attack fallout deepens accountability crisis

title: Day 974: Hamas Al-Qassam Brigades Without Named Supreme Commander for 11th Day — Imad Aqel Remains Last NILI Target as Phase 2 Reconstruction Stalls
detail: On June 7, 2026 (Day 974 / Ceasefire Day 241), Hamas's Al-Qassam Brigades remained without a publicly named supreme military commander for the 11th consecutive day since the IDF's killing of Mohammed Odeh on May 27 — a duration that now exceeds Odeh's entire 9-day tenure. The unprecedented succession vacuum reflects Hamas's strategic calculation that publicly naming any replacement commander would immediately make that person the primary target of the NILI task force's elimination campaign. The NILI task force's systematic campaign against senior October 7 architects has been total among publicly identified figures: Yahya Sinwar (October 16, 2024), Iyad Shambari (April 29, 2026), Izz al-Din al-Haddad (May 16, 2026), and Mohammed Odeh (May 27, 2026) have all been eliminated. Imad Aqel — Hamas's home-front logistics and tunnel-infrastructure commander, born 1971 in Jabaliya — remains the last identified surviving senior Hamas figure from the October 7 planning circle and the NILI task force's primary named remaining target. Israeli analysts have noted Aqel's survival is due to his avoidance of public communications and operational command exposure. Gaza Phase Two ceasefire negotiations remain in complete deadlock on Day 974: the Board of Peace reported reconstruction 'stalled,' less than $1B of $17B pledged received, and Hamas has not accepted disarmament terms. The IDF has documented 3,005+ ceasefire violations; 857+ Palestinians killed since the October 10, 2025 truce began. No new NILI strike was reported on June 6-7.

media.caption: Hamas Qassam Brigades 11 days without named commander — Imad Aqel remains last NILI target as Gaza Phase 2 reconstruction stalls
